> If I compiled it correctly, it didn't help. It was build with `scons platform=android target=template_debug debug_symbols=yes arch=arm64v8` ?

Yeah due to Gradle the Android build setup is still a bit quirky and different from all other platforms.
I believe here you need to add `generate_android_binaries=yes` to SCons (instead of running gradle manually) which should hopefully preserve the debug symbols.

Alternatively, `separate_debug_symbols=yes` will give you a zip with debug symbols, that can be used with `ndk-stack` to symbolicate the stack trace: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/platform/android/resolving_crashes_on_android.html

But again, if you're triggering the crash with 4.6-stable and share the log for that build, anyone can symbolicate the stack trace using the debug symbols from https://github.com/godotengine/godot-builds/releases/download/4.6-stable/Godot_native_debug_symbols.4.6.stable.editor.android.zip

> Is it even touching any code in Godot itself, I guess the bits around libgodot_android?

Yes `libgodot_android.so` is all the Godot code.

If running the gradle manually, i.e not using scons with `separate_debug_symbols` and `generate_android_binaries=yes`, then you need to pass `-PdoNotStrip` to your gradle command, so it doesn't strip symbols.

Without `-PdoNotStrip`, symbols would be seperate.

One thing to note: by default, when Godot runs Gradle to export your app, it'll strip the debug symbols from `libgodot_android.so`

What I usually do is edit the `android/build/gradle.properties` in my Godot project and add this line at the end:

```
# Prevent Gradle from stripping debug symbols.
doNotStrip=true
```

(This is sort of similar to @syntaxerror247's comment, but related to your Godot project exporting, not building Godot itself)
